items.title: Flat out in Andorra with Nina Hoffman, Bodhi Kuhn and Jordi Cortes - The Setup | FOX
items.description:
The dust has barely settled on the La Thuile DH track, but we are already back at it. 
 
Just a few days between rounds to repack the trucks, cross Europe, and do it all over again. For the athletes, their teams, and of course FOX Factory, there is no switching off at this point in the season. You take what you learned last week and get back to work.
 
And there was plenty to take from La Thuile. Asa Vermette, who kicked off the season with that rookie win in Korea, is back on the podium for the third time, finishing second and making it clear he's not going anywhere. Then there's Jackson Goldstone. After a slow start to 2026, he's finally looking like himself again. Third place in La Thuile is a strong signal that the Jackson who closed out 2025 on a tear might just be back.
 
But it wasn't just the front-runners making noise last round. Bodhi Kuhn, who has been building momentum over the last few races, picked up his first career top 10, while Nina Hoffmann backed up a solid Q1 performance with a season-best fifth place. The depth in this field is real. To keep progressing, the limits have to be pushed, and previous success guarantees nothing.
 
Now we are in Pal Arinsal, Andorra, a tiny country in the Pyrenees that punches well above its weight in mountain sports. It's not the steepest track on the calendar, but it's one of the fastest, and with those high speeds, we expect to see some of the tightest margins of the season. Add in the hot weather we're experiencing, and the track should become dusty, blown out, and evolve rapidly from practice through to finals.

#ANDORRA #RIDEFOX #THESETUP

items.title: Lenzerheide World Cup Breakdown | The Season Is Taking Shape
items.description:
Lenzerheide delivered another fascinating weekend of World Cup downhill racing, with Finn Iles securing back-to-back victories, Anna Newkirk claiming the first Elite World Cup win of her career, and Amaury Pierron once again showing why he's one of the fastest riders on the planet. But what did the racing actually tell us about the state of the 2026 season?

In this week's Downtime Podcast Post-Race Show, Chris Kilmurray and Neko Mulally break down all the action from the Lenzerheide UCI Downhill World Cup.

We discuss Finn Iles' growing championship credentials following another impressive victory, Amaury Pierron's blistering pace and the mistakes that may have cost him, and Anna Newkirk's breakthrough performance in the women's race. The conversation also explores the continued progression of the sport, with riders pushing bigger features, tighter margins across the field, and increasing depth in both the men's and women's categories.

As always, expect detailed race analysis, technical insight, paddock observations and plenty of post-race discussion as we look at what Lenzerheide revealed about the riders, teams and storylines shaping the rest of the World Cup season.

Specialized’s new Demo 11 downhill bike is a certified rocket ship. You don’t need us to tell you that. Jordan Williams, Loic Bruni, and Finn Iles have proven the platform's abilities over the past three years of development and this year two World Cup DH wins have been nabbed aboard the production version.
